title: Repair a rule tester
starter:
let int_min = -2147483648
let int_max = 2147483647

let wrap32 (n : int) : int =
  let m = n land 0xFFFFFFFF in
  if m >= 0x80000000 then m - 0x100000000 else m

let add32 (a : int) (b : int) : int = wrap32 (a + b)

let mul32 (a : int) (b : int) : int = a * b

let div32 (a : int) (b : int) : int =
  if b = 0 then -1
  else
    let q = a / b in
    wrap32 (if a mod b <> 0 && (a < 0) <> (b < 0) then q - 1 else q)

let mod32 (a : int) (b : int) : int =
  if b = 0 then a
  else
    let r = a mod b in
    if r <> 0 && (r < 0) <> (b < 0) then r + b else r

let edges = [0; 1; -1]

let breaks (before : int -> 'a) (after : int -> 'a) : int list =
  List.filter (fun x -> before x <> after x) edges

samples.expr: breaks (fun x -> div32 (mul32 x 2) 2) (fun x -> x)
samples.label: breaks (fun x -> div32 (mul32 x 2) 2) (fun x -> x)

samples.expr: breaks (fun x -> add32 (add32 x 3) 4) (fun x -> add32 x 7)
samples.label: breaks (fun x -> add32 (add32 x 3) 4) (fun x -> add32 x 7)

samples.expr: breaks (fun x -> x < add32 x 1) (fun _ -> true)
samples.label: breaks (fun x -> x < add32 x 1) (fun _ -> true)

hints: Run the samples and look at the first one. The tester says the cancel rule never breaks. Every helper except one passes its answer through `wrap32`.
A real i32 multiply keeps only the low 32 bits. Make `mul32` return `wrap32 (a * b)`, the same way `add32` wraps its sum.
A rule can be right for small numbers and wrong at the ends of the i32 range. Add 2 to the 30th, the largest i32 and the smallest i32 to the list: `[0; 1; -1; 1073741824; int_max; int_min]`.

answer.explain: Two repairs. `mul32` has to wrap like the real op, so it returns `wrap32 (a * b)`. Without that the tester does school arithmetic and every rule that is true in school looks safe. The edge list has to hold the values where wrapping happens, so it becomes `[0; 1; -1; 1073741824; int_max; int_min]`. With both fixed, the cancel rule breaks at 1073741824, at the largest i32 and at the smallest i32, and the regroup rule never breaks.
